analysis.investment_thesis: Encompass Design fails both legs of the Magic Formula catastrophically — a P/E of 32.2x implies an earnings yield of only ~3.1%, while a ROE of 0.50% signals the business generates virtually no return on capital. There is no case for owning this at any reasonable price.
key_strengths: Promoter skin in the game at 58.94% — aligned with shareholders
Consumer brand-building theme has secular tailwinds in India
Some institutional presence (FII 7.87% + DII 4.70%) suggests basic liquidity
key_risks: ROE of 0.50% means capital is being destroyed in real terms — ROIC almost certainly sub-5%
Earnings yield ~3.1% (1/32.2x P/E) is less than a risk-free bond — paying growth-stock multiples for a no-growth business
Trading & Distributors is a structurally low-moat, commoditised industry with no pricing power
red_flags: ROE 0.50% — business is essentially earning nothing on shareholder capital
P/E 32.2x with near-zero ROE is an irrational valuation; earnings yield (~3%) is far below my 12% minimum threshold
No positive EBIT story — Magic Formula cannot even be computed meaningfully at these return levels
Market cap INR 347 Cr with ROE <1% screams promoter-driven price inflation, not earnings quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, Encompass Design is a textbook AVOID. The two pillars I require are a high earnings yield (EBIT/EV > 12%) and a high return on capital (ROIC > 20%). Here, the implied earnings yield is roughly 3.1% (inverse of P/E 32.2x, and EBIT-based yield would be marginally higher but nowhere near 12%). More damningly, ROE of 0.50% tells me this business earns virtually nothing on the equity entrusted to it — ROIC is almost certainly in the low single digits. A company that cannot earn more than its cost of capital should never trade at 32x earnings.

The brand-building / consumer distribution story may sound appealing, but the numbers say otherwise. Trading & Distributors is a sector I approach with deep scepticism — thin margins, no proprietary assets, and easy replication. With a market cap of only INR 347 Cr and these fundamentals, this has the hallmarks of a momentum/narrative-driven small-cap rather than a compounding business. Until ROE sustainably crosses 15-20% and the earnings yield becomes attractive, this stock has no place in a Magic Formula portfolio.
